request: Build the Abbaas Ledger designed in the canvas at https://claude.ai/artifact/XpzsEF5ovaU7cB3wYp5bEi as a mobile-friendly website for one owner. The owner sends money to people on Abbaas's behalf, in US dollars or in Maldivian rufiyaa at a rate they type, and Abbaas pays the owner back, usually in dollars. The app records each send and each repayment and shows, in USD, whether Abbaas has the owner's money or the owner has Abbaas's money, and how much. The front end is a static site on GitHub Pages; the backend is Supabase on its free tier, set up the same way as the meals project at /Users/Yuki/Claude/meals. The code lives in a new repository at /Users/Yuki/Claude/abbaas-ledger.

values.observation: On the first visit on a phone the owner signs in once with email and password; every later visit, including opening the app from the home-screen icon, goes straight to Home with no sign-in screen; the ledger belongs to that account, and a second account sees none of its entries or people.

decisions: Reuse analysis binds to nothing: the worktree contains only `.gitignore`, `docs/product/brief.md` and `.nwave/des/` runtime state, so this repository contains no code and every target is CREATE_NEW; the meals project is a separate repository and is therefore a read pattern precedent, never a repository-relative reuse candidate.

Ownership is enforced in Postgres and nowhere else: `people` and `entries` each carry `user_id uuid not null default auth.uid() references auth.users(id) on delete cascade`, have row-level security enabled and per-verb policies `using (auth.uid() = user_id)`, with `revoke all from anon` and explicit grants to `authenticated` and `service_role`. The browser bundle carries no client-side `user_id` filter at all, so deleting a policy makes the oracle fail instead of a client filter quietly hiding the leak.
Value 1 creates BOTH the `people` and `entries` tables, because the observation names both ("none of its entries or people"); later values add columns and screens, never ownership.

The persisted Supabase session IS the session: the client is built with `persistSession: true`, `autoRefreshToken: true`, `detectSessionInUrl: false`, and the app keeps no second copy to fall out of step with it. Measured in `.nwave/des/probe/`: auth-js defaults to `globalThis.localStorage`, a later visit in the same browser restores the stored token and a separate browser does not.

`src/main.ts` resolves the persisted session (`await currentAccount()`) BEFORE the first paint and renders either the sign-in screen or Home, so a returning visit never flashes a sign-in screen; that first-paint ordering, not a redirect afterwards, is what the no-sign-in-screen link observes.

There is no sign-out control (out of scope per `docs/product/brief.md:38`), so the second account is observed on a second phone: a separate browser context with its own origin storage. Measured isolated in `.nwave/des/probe/session-visit-probe.evidence.txt`.

Home at value 1 is the minimal reading surface over the signed-in account's own people and entries, and every element that renders a recorded value carries a stable `data-entry` or `data-person` attribute. The oracle judges ownership on those attributes and never on wording or layout, so value 2 reshaping Home into the two balance boxes cannot falsely break this slice.

An empty ledger and a failed read must never look alike on Home: a LedgerStore read failure renders a named retry notice, because an empty surface that is indistinguishable from a failed read would make the "a second account sees none of it" observation vacuous.

Named failure outcomes live on the ports, not in the UI: refused credentials and a rejected session refresh are Refusals that keep or restore the sign-in screen with their own message; an unreachable auth or REST endpoint is a Retry. A rejected refresh never degrades into a silently empty Home.

Dependency direction is inward: `src/ports/` declares Identity and LedgerStore in domain terms and knows nothing of Supabase; only `src/adapters/supabase/` and `src/main.ts` import `@supabase/supabase-js`; `src/ui/` is functions from state to DOM and imports ports only.

Only the project URL and the anon key reach the bundle, as build-time `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` and `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` that the client refuses to start without. The service-role key exists only in the acceptance support outside the browser and never in the repository.

The local stack takes `project_id = "abbaas-ledger"` and its own port block from 54421 upward, because the meals stack is actually running and holds 54321, 54322, 54324 and 54327 (re-measured with lsof this turn) while 54421-54424 are free; sharing the default block would collide on `supabase start`.

Toolchain is Vite with TypeScript and no UI framework, the Supabase CLI as a devDependency (so `node_modules/.bin` on npm's PATH provides the `supabase` the acceptance support invokes), vitest for unit tests and Playwright for acceptance. The acceptance run drives the BUILT bundle in `dist/` over a real static HTTP origin, so what is judged is what GitHub Pages would serve.

The oracle's test title states the observation verbatim enough to be read without source: the owner signs in once on a phone, a later visit opens straight to Home, and a second account sees none of the ledger.

values.observation: With no entries, Home shows both boxes as empty dashed outlines with $0 (You on the left, Abbaas on the right), an All square chip, a hint to use Send or Receive, a Send button at the bottom left and a Receive button at the bottom right.

values.observation: Tapping Send opens the blue form; the owner enters an amount in USD, picks a paid-to person from the saved list or adds a new one, keeps or changes the date, optionally adds a note, and sees the after-saving boxes; saving returns to Home where the entry sits right of the centre line and Abbaas's box is filled with the new balance, shown without a sign, with the caption has your money.

values.observation: In the send form, switching to MVR shows a rate field (MVR per $1) and the dollar value worked out as the owner types, for example MVR 10,000 at 20.00 shows $500.00; saving stores the MVR amount, the rate and that USD value, and the entry reads MVR 10,000 at 20.00 under its $500.00.

values.observation: Tapping Receive opens the teal form; the owner enters what Abbaas paid (USD, or MVR with a rate), or taps All of it, $500 or $1,000, and sees the after-saving boxes; saving puts the entry left of the centre line and lowers what Abbaas holds. A payment larger than he holds shows a note before saving and, once saved, empties his box and fills the owner's blue box with the difference and the caption have his money; a payment equal to what he holds leaves both boxes empty and shows All square.
